answer:
The first century in which Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends — Pottery Decoration increasing significantly while Pottery Form declines simultaneously — is the century 1800–1700 BCE (CE −1800 → −1700, conventionally the 18th century BCE).

Data basis (executed analysis, analysis/answer.py): using the cross-file identical Z-series (PotteryForm = capital.ZKeform; PotteryDecoration = capital.Zkeverz; CE = −BCE; raw = interpolated at anchors), and century-over-century growth on the data's 100-yr anchor grid, the qualifying century shows Pottery Form falling 1.87 Z (from +0.74 to −1.13) while Pottery Decoration rises 1.45 Z (from −0.48 to +0.97). These are −3.33 SD and +3.36 SD of the century-to-century changes (and −1.89/+1.58 SD of the series levels) — far beyond the 1-SD significance threshold and the permissive 0.5-Z threshold.

This is the FIRST qualifying century: a chronological scan from 4100 BCE shows that in every earlier century the two series move in the same direction (or are flat); 1800–1700 BCE is the only opposite-direction interval over the entire 4100–500 BCE span. Robustness cross-checks agree: (A) within-century OLS slopes on the yearly interpolated series identify 1800–1700 BCE as the sole qualifying century (slopes −0.0187/yr for Form, +0.0145/yr for Decoration); (B) a phase-free sliding 100-yr window first reaches significance starting at CE −1864 (spanning 1864–1764 BCE) — the same isolated divergence event, with only ±0.007 Z (numerical noise, not significant) in any earlier window. The conclusion is therefore robust to century-labeling convention: whether it is phrased "the 18th century BCE," "1800–1700 BCE," or "around 1700 BCE," it refers to the same single, decisive divergence — no earlier century qualifies under any reading with the significance criterion.

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form first show opposite growth trends in the century 1800–1700 BCE (18th century BCE): Pottery Decoration rises significantly (+1.45 Z) while Pottery Form declines (−1.87 Z), the only such opposite-direction century across 4100–500 BCE.
payload.workflow: 1) Validate variable mapping (PotteryForm==ZKeform, PotteryDecoration==Zkeverz, CE=−BCE, raw==_inter at anchors). 2) Compute century-over-century Z changes on the raw 100-yr anchors; scan chronologically for first century with dDec>0 & dForm<0 exceeding 1 SD of century changes (and 0.5-Z permissive threshold). 3) Cross-check A: within-century OLS slopes on interpolated yearly series. 4) Cross-check B: phase-free sliding 100-yr window on interpolated series. 5) Report per-century summary table and final natural-language answer with explicit BCE interval and effect sizes. Supporting artifacts: analysis/per_century_summary.csv, analysis/plan_inspection.py, analysis/crosscheck_B_debug.py.
